headword: {懐石料理|かいせきりょうり}

definitions.gloss: kaiseki; multi-course meal of the tea ceremony
definitions.explanation: A light meal of small, seasonal dishes served before tea at a formal tea gathering; by extension, a refined multi-course Japanese meal.

examples.japanese: {懐石料理|かいせきりょうり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦いただく→いただく：01326_itadaku⟧。
⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{本格的|ほんかくてき}→本格的：05681_honkakuteki⟧な{懐石料理|かいせきりょうり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{味|あじ}わった→味わう：04405_ajiwau⟧。
examples.english: I enjoyed authentic kaiseki cuisine in Kyoto.

examples.japanese: {懐石料理|かいせきりょうり}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食材|しょくざい}→食材：04940_shokuzai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦ずつ→〜ずつ：03092_zutsu⟧⟦{美|うつく}しく→美しい：01121_utsukushii⟧⟦{盛|も}り{付|つ}ける→盛り付ける：14764_moritsukeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{特徴|とくちょう}→特徴：03456_tokuchou⟧だ。
examples.english: Kaiseki is known for small, beautifully arranged portions of seasonal ingredients.

notes:
Often shortened to ⟦{懐石|かいせき}→懐石：12635_kaiseki⟧. The name comes from the warm stone (⟦{石|いし}→石：02177_ishi⟧) Zen monks are said to have held to their chest (⟦{懐|ふところ}→懐：12631_futokoro⟧) to ease hunger, hence a light meal.

WATCH OUT:
⟦{会席料理|かいせきりょうり}→会席料理：26980_kaisekiryouri⟧ has the same reading but means a banquet course meal served with sake at inns and restaurants. Menus often mix the two, but strictly ⟦{懐石|かいせき}→懐石：12635_kaiseki⟧ comes before tea and ⟦{会席|かいせき}→会席：11648_kaiseki⟧ accompanies drinking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {懐石料理|かいせきりょうり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧: kaiseki restaurant
- {茶懐石|ちゃかいせき}: tea-ceremony kaiseki
